title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics and bump versions to v1.40.0
author: Priya Kapoor
body: Context: Multiple SDKs (python/typescript/go) had diverging semantics for auth, retry/backoff defaults, and streaming ergonomics which made cross-language parity and docs confusing. This PR unifies the behavior across SDKs, adds ergonomics improvements for streaming usage, and performs a coordinated version bump to v1.40.0 for all SDK packages. Summary of changes: 1) Auth: unified credential resolution order (env -> config file -> explicit client param), consistent env var names (REDWOOD_API_KEY / REDWOOD_TOKEN), and automated short-lived token refresh helper for hosted credentials. 2) Retries: standardized default retry policy (idempotent-only retries, exponential backoff with jitter, 3 max attempts for 5xx/network, 0 for non-idempotent by default), and exposed RetryPolicy object for advanced configuration. 3) Streaming APIs: consistent streaming interfaces across languages: Python gains async iterator and context manager for stream responses, TypeScript adds EventEmitter-style stream helper plus async iterator, Go exposes a StreamClient with Recv/Close semantics with improved cancellation. 4) Ergonomics: improved error types (Typed SDKError with codes), simplified client construction helpers (from_env(), from_api_key()), and better typed docs/examples. 5) Parity fixes: small protocol fixes to ensure chunk framing and metadata fields are identical across SDKs. 6) Version bump: python/ts/go packages to v1.40.0 with coordinated changelogs. Backwards compatibility: default behaviors changed only in the direction of stricter retry semantics and more explicit streaming helpers; most old call patterns still work but some streaming helper method names were renamed to improve clarity (aliases kept for one release). Migration notes: - Python: prefer replacing Response.stream_raw() with Response.stream() async iterator; alias kept but deprecated. - TS: new StreamHelper.on('chunk') API is recommended. - Go: use StreamClient.Recv(ctx) and defer StreamClient.Close(). Testing: added cross-language conformance tests in eval-harness and unit tests per SDK. CI: cross-repo integration matrix run (python/ts/go) and e2e streaming replay harness. Related: Linear ENG-3421, ENG-3580. Checklist: - [x] Design doc completed and reviewed - [x] SDK implementations updated - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Updated docs and examples - [x] Changelogs and version bumps - [x] CI green (post-fix) Impact: Simplifies multi-language adoption, reduces support burden, and fixes a class of streaming framing bugs seen in production. Rollout: released as coordinated minor across all languages; monitor metrics for increased client-side 429/500s and streaming error rates for 72 hours.

review_comments: Tomás Rivera (reviewer): Left a couple of nits on the TS API surface - can we rename 'onChunk' to 'on' with event types to match node streams? Also please add a deprecation note for the old helper.
Priya Kapoor (author): Addressed - switched to StreamHelper.on(event, cb) and added deprecation alias + doc note. Replying to Tomas: PTAL at commit c3e5f90.
Evelyn Zhang (reviewer): Great work. Two requests: add explicit tests for token refresh race and verify client construction from config file works in CI matrix.
Priya Kapoor (author): Added token-refresh race tests and config-file sanity checks in python/ and go/ integration jobs (see e5a7b34).
Marcus Lee (reviewer): CI flakes on the TS streaming e2e - root cause was missing backpressure handling; fixed in b2d4e8f and retried CI.
CI Bot: integration/python passed on run #3; typescript flaky test fixed and passed; go integration passed.
release_notes: v1.40.0: Unify auth credential resolution and short-lived token refresh helpers across SDKs.
v1.40.0: Standardize retry/backoff defaults and expose RetryPolicy for custom policies.
v1.40.0: Improve streaming ergonomics: Python async iterator, TS StreamHelper, Go StreamClient.
v1.40.0: Parity fixes for chunk framing and metadata fields across SDKs.
Migration: see docs/sdk/migration.md for minor API changes and deprecation timeline.
